Fetched persons:10000, 65131 ms\r\n```\r\n\r\n**Further investigation**\r\nCentral to the most time consuming operation, the fetching of Java objects for the result, is the method `BaseAdoService.getByIds`. Here, once the list of ids to fetch is established, a query of the following form is executed:\r\n```sql\r\nselect\r\n  \u003clist of attributes\u003e\r\n    from\r\n        Person person0_ \r\n    where\r\n        person0_.id in (\u003clist of Ids\u003e)\r\n    order by\r\n        person0_.changeDate asc,\r\n        person0_.uuid asc,\r\n        person0_.id asc;\r\n```\r\nThe duration of this initial query is neglectible (~38ms for 1000 ids, ~118ms for 10000 ids). Notable is, however, the number of individual queries executed for the overall execution of `getAllAfter`, which is 3041 for 1000 ids and 30104 for 10000 ids. This indicates a bottleneck in Hibernate's fetching of Java objects, with a number of queries linear to the number of objects to be fetched.\r\n\r\nFor a batch limit of 10000, the following execution times of individual queries are logged:\r\n- 8151.854 ms\r\n- 952.298 ms\r\n- 814.055 ms\r\n- 136.874 ms\r\n- 92.417 ms\r\n- 37.419 ms\r\n- 34.018 ms\r\n- 9.336 ms\r\n- 1.036 ms\r\n- 0.766 ms\r\n- 0.738 ms\r\n- 0.723 ms\r\n- 0.662 ms\r\n...\r\n\r\nThat is, a few longer running queries (most of which are clearly recognizeable in the measurements above) are followed by a large number of queries below 1ms.\r\n\r\n\u003c/details\u003e\r\n\r\n**Conclusion**:\r\n1. The refactoring has a huge impact both for smaller batch sizes (1m 19.47s down to 13. 79 for batch size 1000) and for bigger batch sizes (3m 3.19s down to 1m 11.64s for batch size 10000).\r\n2. Only selecting the ids (with uuid and changeDate for sorting) brings a big improvement.\r\n3. Not fetching persons that are above the batch limit is a waste of load time that we now avoid. Postponing fetching to a sorted and already reduced list of previously queried attributes has a huge impact for larger batches, too.\r\n4. The perfomance improvement introduced through indices is especially relevant for smaller batch sizes.\r\n5. Adding `HINT_HIBERNATE_READ_ONLY` does not seem to make a notable difference. Execution time was even worse for batch size 10000, however not at a scale that cannot be attributed to differences in system workload.\r\n6. Overall, now most of the time is spent on fetching JPA entities and a bit overhead to convert them to DTOs.","bodyHTML":"\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003ePerformance Here, once the list of ids to fetch is established, a query of the following form is executed:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"highlight highlight-source-sql notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" dir=\"auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"select\n  \u0026lt;list of attributes\u0026gt;\n    from\n        Person person0_ \n    where\n        person0_.id in (\u0026lt;list of Ids\u0026gt;)\n    order by\n        person0_.changeDate asc,\n        person0_.uuid asc,\n        person0_.id asc;\"\u003e\u003cpre class=\"notranslate\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003eselect\u003c/span\u003e\n  \u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003e\u0026lt;\u003c/span\u003elist of attributes\u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003e\u0026gt;\u003c/span\u003e\n    \u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003efrom\u003c/span\u003e\n        Person person0_ \n    \u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003ewhere\u003c/span\u003e\n        \u003cspan class=\"pl-c1\"\u003eperson0_\u003c/span\u003e.\u003cspan class=\"pl-c1\"\u003eid\u003c/span\u003e \u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003ein\u003c/span\u003e (\u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003e\u0026lt;\u003c/span\u003elist of Ids\u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003e\u0026gt;\u003c/span\u003e)\n    \u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003eorder by\u003c/span\u003e\n        \u003cspan class=\"pl-c1\"\u003eperson0_\u003c/span\u003e.\u003cspan class=\"pl-c1\"\u003echangeDate\u003c/span\u003e \u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003easc\u003c/span\u003e,\n        \u003cspan class=\"pl-c1\"\u003eperson0_\u003c/span\u003e.\u003cspan class=\"pl-c1\"\u003euuid\u003c/span\u003e \u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003easc\u003c/span\u003e,\n        \u003cspan class=\"pl-c1\"\u003eperson0_\u003c/span\u003e.\u003cspan class=\"pl-c1\"\u003eid\u003c/span\u003e \u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003easc\u003c/span\u003e;\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe duration of this initial query is neglectible (~38ms for 1000 ids, ~118ms for 10000 ids). Notable is, however, the number of individual queries executed for the overall execution of \u003ccode class=\"notranslate\"\u003egetAllAfter\u003c/code\u003e, which is 3041 for 1000 ids and 30104 for 10000 ids. This indicates a bottleneck in Hibernate's fetching of Java objects, with a number of queries linear to the number of objects to be fetched.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eFor a batch limit of 10000, the following execution times of individual queries are logged:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e8151.854 ms\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e952.298 ms\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e814.055 ms\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e136.874 ms\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e92.417 ms\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e37.419 ms\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e34.018 ms\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e9.336 ms\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e1.036 ms\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e0.766 ms\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e0.738 ms\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e0.723 ms\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e0.662 ms\u003cbr\u003e\n...\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThat is, a few longer running queries (most of which are clearly recognizeable in the measurements above) are followed by a large number of queries below 1ms.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/details\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eConclusion\u003c/strong\u003e:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003col dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eThe refactoring has a huge impact both for smaller batch sizes (1m 19.47s down to 13. 79 for batch size 1000) and for bigger batch sizes (3m 3.19s down to 1m 11.64s for batch size 10000).\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eOnly selecting the ids (with uuid and changeDate for sorting) brings a big improvement.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eNot fetching persons that are above the batch limit is a waste of load time that we now avoid. Postponing fetching to a sorted and already reduced list of previously queried attributes has a huge impact for larger batches, too.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eThe perfomance improvement introduced through indices is especially relevant for smaller batch sizes.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eAdding \u003ccode class=\"notranslate\"\u003eHINT_HIBERNATE_READ_ONLY\u003c/code\u003e does not seem to make a notable difference. Execution time was even worse for batch size 10000, however not at a scale that cannot be attributed to differences in system workload.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eOverall, now most of the time is spent on fetching JPA entities and a bit overhead to convert them to You don't have to remove this comment or any other comment from this issue as they will automatically be hidden.\r\n-->\r\n### Problem Description\r\nIn the REST API, `getAllAfter` methods tend to be slow for large numbers of entities to be sent, up to possible timeouts.\r\nSee **Additional Information** for a detailed analysis.\r\n\r\n### Proposed Change\r\n\r\nFor this issue we should only work on improving PersonService.getAllAfter.\r\n\r\n- [x] Instead of directly querying the whole Person, only query for id, uuid and changeDate in PersonService.getAllAfter for immunizations, cases, etc. Unify, sort, distinct and limit the combined results of those queries. <h3 dir="auto">Problem Description</h3>
<p dir="auto">In the REST API, <code class="notranslate">getAllAfter</code> methods tend to be slow for large numbers of entities to be sent, up to possible timeouts.<br>
See <strong>Additional Information</strong> for a detailed analysis.</p>
<h3 dir="auto">Proposed Change</h3>
<p dir="auto">For this issue we should only work on improving PersonService.getAllAfter.</p>
<ul class="contains-task-list">
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" id="" disabled="" class="task-list-item-checkbox" aria-label="Completed task" checked=""> Instead of directly querying the whole Person, only query for id, uuid and changeDate in PersonService.getAllAfter for immunizations, cases, etc. Unify, sort, distinct and limit the combined results of those queries. Use the ids to query for the actual persons - here try to fetch all needed data directly to mitigate lazy loading queries.</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" id="" disabled="" class="task-list-item-checkbox" aria-label="Completed task" checked=""> Add the following indices. Make sure cases, etc. also have the index for person_id</li>
</ul>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="  CREATE INDEX idx_person_changedate_uuid_id ON public.person USING btree (changedate ASC, uuid ASC, id ASC);
  CREATE INDEX idx_immunization_person ON public.immunization USING btree (person_id);"><pre class="notranslate"><code class="notranslate">  CREATE INDEX idx_person_changedate_uuid_id ON public.person USING btree (changedate ASC, uuid ASC, id ASC);
  CREATE INDEX idx_immunization_person ON public.immunization USING btree (person_id);
</code></pre></div>
<ul class="contains-task-list">
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" id="" disabled="" class="task-list-item-checkbox" aria-label="Completed task" checked=""> If this works out correct, get in contact with <a class="user-mention notranslate" data-hovercard-type="user" data-hovercard-url="/users/StefanKock/hovercard" data-octo-click="hovercard-link-click" data-octo-dimensions="link_type:self" href="https://github.com/StefanKock">@StefanKock</a> or <a class="user-mention notranslate" data-hovercard-type="user" data-hovercard-url="/users/MartinWahnschaffe/hovercard" data-octo-click="hovercard-link-click" data-octo-dimensions="link_type:self" href="https://github.com/MartinWahnschaffe">@MartinWahnschaffe</a> to create a follow-up issue for getAllAfter methods of other entities. -> <span class="reference"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-issue-closed closed mr-1" title="Closed" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M11.28 6.78a.75.75 0 0 0-1.06-1.06L7.25 8.69 5.78 7.22a.75.75 0 0 0-1.06 1.06l2 2a.75.75 0 0 0 1.06 0l3.5-3.5Z"></path><path d="M16 8A8 8 0 1 1 0 8a8 8 0 0 1 16 0Zm-1.5 0a6.5 6.5 0 1 0-13 0 6.5 6.5 0 0 0 13 0Z"></path></svg><a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="1246489465" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/SORMAS-Foundation/SORMAS-Project/issues/9320" data-hovercard-type="issue" data-hovercard-url="/SORMAS-Foundation/SORMAS-Project/issues/9320/hovercard" href="https://github.com/SORMAS-Foundation/SORMAS-Project/issues/9320">Improve performance of getAllAfter queries into DTOs [8]<span class="issue-shorthand"> #9320</span></a></span></li>
</ul>
<h3 dir="auto">System Details</h3>

<ul dir="auto">
<li>Device:</li>
<li>SORMAS version: 1.71.0-SNAPSHOT</li>
<li>Android version/Browser:</li>
<li>Server URL:</li>
<li>User Role: Rest User</li>
</ul>
<h3 dir="auto">Additional Information</h3>

<p dir="auto">Also check this comment for an analysis including explain analyze results: <a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="1214898760" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/SORMAS-Foundation/SORMAS-Project/issues/8946" data-hovercard-type="issue" data-hovercard-url="/SORMAS-Foundation/SORMAS-Project/issues/8946/hovercard?comment_id=1129937176&comment_type=issue_comment" href="https://github.com/SORMAS-Foundation/SORMAS-Project/issues/8946#issuecomment-1129937176">#8946 (comment)</a></p>
<p dir="auto">See first analysis for an overview on runtimes for different REST methods.</p>
<p dir="auto">Some additional research on <code class="notranslate">PersonService.getAllAfter</code> shows:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>joins on large tables (> 1000000 entries) result in exceptional query runtimes, increased by factor ~2 by redundancies introduced by hibernate</li>
<li>adding indexes results in medium improvement</li>
<li>hibernate fetching has a relevant effect for  large batch sizes, even without single queries with exceptional runtimes</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Note:</strong> testes version has progressed to 1.72.0-SNAPSHOT</p>

<p dir="auto">The following measurements were taken from backend logs (EJB methods) and the Postgres logs.<br>
Observations:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>the actual SQL queries are executed in few seconds while the EJB methods take minutes to complete</li>

<li>batch size is relevant. Some requests did not complete within reasonable time for a batch size of 10000, these were measured for batch size 1000.</li>
</ul>

The instrumented version was executed to fetch 10, 1000 or 10000 entries.<br>
(Note: tested version has been progressed to 1.72.0-SNAPSHOT, some of the database entries have been deleted by automated deletion)</p>
<p dir="auto">Result:<br>
<a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow" href="https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5616564/168072723-56a92b63-b763-4eed-9e45-a826aae66504.png"><img src="https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5616564/168072723-56a92b63-b763-4eed-9e45-a826aae66504.png" alt="image" style="max-width: 100%;"></a></p>
<p dir="auto">Notable is that the times spent for immunization are much closer for the different batch sizes (70470 to 83377 ms) while the other steps show greater variations (e.g., 2409 to 38397 ms for district) which can likely be attributed to hibernate fetching, i.e., after identifying the entities to be retrieved (which is usually a longer running query) to fetch dependent subentities and fill missing data.</p>
<p dir="auto">Analysis of the SQL log for the run of 1000 entries shows one particularly long running query (70913.899 ms) while all others remain in a range clearly below 10000 ms (or 10 seconds). dir="auto">I've had another look at this and have the following findings:</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>Original query with the performance test database and a limit to 100 took 1m11s: <a href="https://explain.dalibo.com/plan/Zwh" rel="nofollow">https://explain.dalibo.com/plan/Zwh</a></li>
<li>Removed fetch immunizationPersonsSelect.fetch(Person.ADDRESS) changes it to 25s: <a href="https://explain.dalibo.com/plan/HIq#plan" rel="nofollow">https://explain.dalibo.com/plan/HIq#plan</a><br>
It's not clear to me why we need this here. My guess is that we can get rid of it, but this needs to be tested more thoroughly</li>
<li>Limiting the query to just id, uuid and changedate reduces it to 9s: <a href="https://explain.dalibo.com/plan/8frT#plan" rel="nofollow">https://explain.dalibo.com/plan/8frT#plan</a><br>
The idea here is to do this for all the queries done in PersonService.getAllAfter, then order and limit the results and afterwards only query the specific persons needed, using the ids (and batching).</li>
<li>Introducing indices finally reduces the query time to 19ms (!): <a href="https://explain.dalibo.com/plan/NY2" rel="nofollow">https://explain.dalibo.com/plan/NY2</a></li>
</ol>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="  CREATE INDEX idx_person_changedate_uuid_id ON public.person USING btree (changedate ASC, uuid ASC, id ASC);
  CREATE INDEX idx_immunization_person ON public.immunization USING btree (person_id);"><pre class="notranslate"><code class="notranslate">  CREATE INDEX idx_person_changedate_uuid_id ON public.person USING btree (changedate ASC, uuid ASC, id ASC);
  CREATE INDEX idx_immunization_person ON public.immunization USING btree (person_id);
</code></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Querying the actual data afterwards also only takes a few milliseconds: <a href="https://explain.dalibo.com/plan/bnEc" rel="nofollow">https://explain.dalibo.com/plan/bnEc</a></p>
<p dir="auto">Suggested todos:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Instead of directly querying the whole Person, only query for id, uuid and changeDate in PersonService.getAllAfter for immunizations, cases, etc. Unify, sort, distinct and limit the combined results of those queries. Use the ids to query for the actual persons - here try to fetch all needed data directly to mitigate lazy loading queries.</li>

<p dir="auto"><strong>Further investigation</strong><br>
Central to the most time consuming operation, the fetching of Java objects for the result, is the method <code class="notranslate">BaseAdoService.getByIds</code>. Here, once the list of ids to fetch is established, a query of the following form is executed:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-sql notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="select
  <list of attributes>
    from
        Person person0_ 
    where
        person0_.id in (<list of Ids>)
    order by
        person0_.changeDate asc,
        person0_.uuid asc,
        person0_.id asc;"><pre class="notranslate"><span class="pl-k">select</span>
  <span class="pl-k"><</span>list of attributes<span class="pl-k">></span>
    <span class="pl-k">from</span>
        Person person0_ 
    <span class="pl-k">where</span>
        <span class="pl-c1">person0_</span>.<span class="pl-c1">id</span> <span class="pl-k">in</span> (<span class="pl-k"><</span>list of Ids<span class="pl-k">></span>)
    <span class="pl-k">order by</span>
        <span class="pl-c1">person0_</span>.<span class="pl-c1">changeDate</span> <span class="pl-k">asc</span>,
        <span class="pl-c1">person0_</span>.<span class="pl-c1">uuid</span> <span class="pl-k">asc</span>,
        <span class="pl-c1">person0_</span>.<span class="pl-c1">id</span> <span class="pl-k">asc</span>;</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">The duration of this initial query is neglectible (~38ms for 1000 ids, ~118ms for 10000 ids). Notable is, however, the number of individual queries executed for the overall execution of <code class="notranslate">getAllAfter</code>, which is 3041 for 1000 ids and 30104 for 10000 ids. This indicates a bottleneck in Hibernate's fetching of Java objects, with a number of queries linear to the number of objects to be fetched.</p>
<p dir="auto">For a batch limit of 10000, the following execution times of individual queries are logged:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>8151.854 ms</li>
<li>952.298 ms</li>
<li>814.055 ms</li>
<li>136.874 ms</li>
<li>92.417 ms</li>
<li>37.419 ms</li>
<li>34.018 ms</li>
<li>9.336 ms</li>
<li>1.036 ms</li>
<li>0.766 ms</li>
<li>0.738 ms</li>

...</li>

<p dir="auto">That is, a few longer running queries (most of which are clearly recognizeable in the measurements above) are followed by a large number of queries below 1ms.</p>
</details>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Conclusion</strong>:</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>The refactoring has a huge impact both for smaller batch sizes (1m 19.47s down to 13. 79 for batch size 1000) and for bigger batch sizes (3m 3.19s down to 1m 11.64s for batch size 10000).</li>
<li>Only selecting the ids (with uuid and changeDate for sorting) brings a big improvement.</li>
<li>Not fetching persons that are above the batch limit is a waste of load time that we now avoid. Postponing fetching to a sorted and already reduced list of previously queried attributes has a huge impact for larger batches, too.</li>
<li>The perfomance improvement introduced through indices is especially relevant for smaller batch sizes.</li>
<li>Adding <code class="notranslate">HINT_HIBERNATE_READ_ONLY</code> does not seem to make a notable difference. Execution time was even worse for batch size 10000, however not at a scale that cannot be attributed to differences in system workload.</li>
<li>Overall, now most of the time is spent on fetching JPA entities and a bit overhead to convert them to DTOs.</li>
